🚨 What happens when an AI model gets too good at finding software vulnerabilities?

Z.ai aimed to build a stronger coding assistant with GLM-5.3. By using advanced reinforcement learning on simulated developer environments, they succeeded.

But they also got something unexpected: a model highly capable of discovering and exploiting security flaws. It more than doubled its predecessor's score on ExploitBench. The results were so powerful that Z.ai delayed releasing the open weights to conduct thorough safety testing.

🗑️ Stop letting your AI agents forget crucial details to save on compute costs!

Usually, when an AI context window gets full, the system just deletes the oldest messages. Researchers at Xiaohongshu introduced a new approach with a method called Self-GC.

It uses a planner LLM to intelligently fold, mask, or prune data. This keeps long-running agents affordable without making them forgetful.

🔍 Why did DeepSeek just release the exact harness it uses to train and test their AI?

When evaluating AI agents, the environment matters just as much as the model.

DeepSeek just launched DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, but they also open sourced their agentic scaffolding: DeepSeek Harness.

This tool logs everything an AI ingests, meaning any session can be searched, forked, or completely replayed. For developers, this means you can reproduce the performance measured by official benchmark numbers on your own hardware instead of trusting closed evaluations.

⚡ Why is speed becoming one of the most crucial metrics in AI development?

Some developers only track two main metrics: accuracy and cost. But new releases from OpenAI, Cerebras, Google, and Nvidia put the spotlight on a third factor: speed.

Understanding the difference between two key measurements of speed is essential:
⏱️ Latency: The wait time before the first token appears.
🚀 Throughput: How many tokens the model generates per second once it starts.

Too often, vibe coded applications built without underlying software knowledge hit bottlenecks at scale. Using coding agents may reduce the need to memorize a language’s syntax, but developers still have to weigh system-level trade-offs for themselves.

In the latest issue of The Batch, Andrew Ng breaks down the 5 core engineering fundamentals needed to build applications effectively:

💻 Full-Stack Systems: Overseeing rendering, state management, and API design.
🗃️ Data Architecture: Structuring storage types and schemas for information.
🛠️ System Design: Setting boundaries, selecting frame

Building robust AI applications requires steering coding agents through complex trade-offs. Latency, data management, and infrastructure cost all matter more when applications scale. How do you learn these foundations?

This week in The Batch:

▪️ Andrew Ng explains why software engineering fundamentals remain critical for developers building AI and AI-aided applications.
▪️ GLM-5.3 shows off powerful exploit detection, with open weights released post-evaluation.

An LLM generates text one token at a time, and each token depends on the keys and values of every previous one, stored in the KV cache. Older systems reserved one contiguous slab per request sized for max context length, and most of it sat empty.

Paged attention splits the cache into small fixed-size blocks scattered anywhere in GPU memory, with a lookup table tracking where they live. Watch the clip for the full breakdown.
